**Issue #1569 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1569: Patch: the challenge dialog and popups take, hold and return keyboard focus
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The "Challenge a friend" dialog claims to be a modal to assistive technology but doesn't act like one: when it opens, keyboard focus stays on the button behind the dimmed page, pressing Escape does nothing until something inside is clicked, and Tab can walk out of it onto the page behind. The portrait picker and the in-match chat have the mirror-image problem — closing them drops focus to the page body, so a keyboard user loses their place. After this, opening the dialog focuses it, Escape and Tab behave as a modal's should, and closing any of the three returns focus to the control that opened it.

## Why
`together/ChallengeDialog.tsx:110-128` declares `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` but never moves focus in, has no Tab trap, and binds Escape on the form's own `onKeyDown` — dead until an inner control happens to have focus. `settings/SettingsPanel.tsx:158-213` and `cards/inspect/store.ts`'s `useModalOverlay` already implement focus-in, trap, Escape and restore correctly (the card drill-down was fixed to them in #1527); `emotes/PortraitPicker.tsx` and the `InMatchChat`/`ChatPanel` close path do neither. Open issue #1561 extends the automated axe scan to more routes, but axe audits DOM attributes — it cannot catch a modal that never takes focus or a close that strands it. This is the behavioral half.

## Proposal
Give `ChallengeDialog` the `useModalOverlay` (or SettingsPanel-style) treatment: focus the dialog on open, trap Tab, Escape closes from any focus position, focus returns to the Challenge button on close; restore focus to the triggering control on `PortraitPicker` close and in-match chat close, and pair `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` where those toggles already claim them.

## Where it lands
`apps/web/src/together/{ChallengeDialog,InMatchChat,ChatPanel}.tsx`, `apps/web/src/emotes/PortraitPicker.tsx`; reference implementations `apps/web/src/settings/SettingsPanel.tsx`, `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opening the challenge dialog moves focus inside it; Tab cycles within; Escape closes from anywhere; closing returns focus to the trigger
- [ ] Closing the portrait picker or the in-match chat returns focus to the control that opened it
- [ ] Component tests in the shape of the #1527 drill-down tests

## Size and risks
Medium; client-only, reuses existing overlay machinery. Risk is regressing the dialog's submit flow — covered by the existing challenge e2e/component tests.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/39663611565)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`ChallengeDialog` acts as the modal it claims to be. When it opens, the focus moves to its checked mode radio. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside it and never reach the page behind. Escape closes it wherever the focus is. Every way of closing it (Escape, Cancel, the scrim, a sent challenge) gives the focus back to the friend row's Challenge button that opened it.

Closing the portrait picker by Escape or by a pick gives the focus back to its portrait button, and closing the in-match chat conversation gives the focus back to the board rail's Chat toggle. The toggles that already carry `aria-expanded` (the in-match Chat toggle, the portrait button, each Preview) also carry `aria-controls` while expanded. Component tests in the shape of #1527's (`apps/web/src/routes/stats.test.tsx`, "the card drill-down dialog") prove each part.

This was prototyped in a throwaway worktree, which has since been deleted. There, the code and tests below passed: 75 tests in the three files, the 31 related files under `--changed`, `tsc` and eslint. Against the unchanged source, 8 of the 9 new tests fail.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/together/ChallengeDialog.tsx` | change | header comment; `TAB_STOPS`, `tabStops()`; `dialog` ref on the form; focus-on-open effect; window keydown effect; the form's `onKeyDown` removed |
| `apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.tsx` | change | `FriendRowProps.onChallenge(opener)`; `challengeOpener` ref, `closeChallenge()`; the dialog's `onClose`/`onSent` |
| `apps/web/src/together/InMatchChat.tsx` | change | `toggle` ref, `listId`; `aria-controls`; the `ChatPanel` `onClose` focuses the toggle |
| `apps/web/src/emotes/PortraitPicker.tsx` | change | `toggle` ref, `menuId`, `panelId`; Escape and a pick focus the portrait button; `aria-controls`; `PortraitTile` gains `panelId` |
| `apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.test.tsx` | change | `TESTID` entries, `press()`, a new describe with 4 tests |
| `apps/web/src/together/ChatPanel.test.tsx` | change | 1 test |
| `apps/web/src/emotes/PortraitPicker.test.tsx` | change | a new describe with 4 tests |

**Do not touch:**
- `apps/web/src/together/ChatPanel.tsx`: its input focus and Escape already work, and the restore is the caller's.
- `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts`, `apps/web/src/settings/SettingsPanel.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/stats.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckCosmeticsPicker.tsx`.
- Any CSS, `e2e/`, `crates/`, `spec/`, any `package.json`.

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is client UX only: nothing here decides a rule or shows hidden information (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Put no R-number in any new code, comment or test title.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/together/ChallengeDialog.tsx`.** Copy the pattern of `apps/web/src/game/ConfirmConcede.tsx`, which has two effects.
   - Header: after the line ending "whether a deck may be played is the server's, at the room.", add `//`, then:
     ```
     // A modal like the client's others (`game/ConfirmConcede.tsx`, #1569): the focus moves to the checked
     // mode when it opens, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside, Escape closes it wherever the focus is, and the
     // caller gives the focus back to the Challenge button that opened it (`TogetherRoute.tsx`).
     ```
   - Add `useRef` to the `react` import.
   - After `type Saved = …`, add:
     ```ts
     /** What Tab may land on in the dialog. */
     const TAB_STOPS = "a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled])";

     /** The dialog's tab stops in order; the mode group is one stop, its checked radio, as the browser's own Tab takes it. */
     function tabStops(dialog: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] {
       return [...dialog.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(TAB_STOPS)].filter(
         (element) => !(element instanceof HTMLInputElement && element.type === "radio" && !element.checked),
       );
     }
     ```
   - In `ChallengeDialog`, after `const [error, setError] = …` and before the `getDecks` effect, add:
     ```ts
     const dialog = useRef<HTMLFormElement>(null);

     // Keyboard and screen-reader users start inside the dialog, on the mode it opens with.
     useEffect(() => {
       const form = dialog.current;
       if (form !== null) tabStops(form)[0]?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
     }, []);

     // Both keys are read at the window, in the capture phase, so they hold wherever the focus is (a
     // click on the dialog's text or the dimmed page takes it off the controls): Escape closes, and Tab
     // and Shift+Tab step through the dialog's stops, wrapping, never onto the page behind the scrim.
     useEffect(() => {
       function onKey(event: globalThis.KeyboardEvent): void {
         if (event.key === "Escape") {
           event.preventDefault();
           event.stopPropagation();
           onClose();
           return;
         }
         if (event.key !== "Tab") return;
         const form = dialog.current;
         if (form === null) return;
         const order = tabStops(form);
         if (order.length === 0) return;
         const focused = document.activeElement;
         const at = focused instanceof HTMLElement ? order.indexOf(focused) : -1;
         const next = event.shiftKey ? (at <= 0 ? order.length - 1 : at - 1) : at === order.length - 1 ? 0 : at + 1;
         event.preventDefault();
         event.stopPropagation();
         order[next]?.focus();
       }
       window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true);
       return () => {
         window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey, true);
       };
     }, [onClose]);
     ```
   - On the `<form>`, add `ref={dialog}` as its first prop. Delete its whole `onKeyDown={…}` prop. Change nothing else in the JSX: no `tabIndex`, and leave the scrim's `onClick`, `onSubmit={send}`, `aria-modal` and `aria-labelledby` as they are.

2. **`apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.tsx`.**
   - Add `useRef` to the `react` import.
   - In `FriendRowProps`, replace `onChallenge: () => void;` with:
     ```ts
     /** Gets the Challenge button pressed, which has the focus back once the dialog closes. */
     onChallenge: (opener: HTMLElement) => void;
     ```
   - In `FriendRow`, rewrite the Challenge `<button>` over several lines. Keep `type="button"`, `className="button-primary"`, `data-testid={togetherTestid.challenge}` and `disabled={busy}`. Set `onClick={(event) => { onChallenge(event.currentTarget); }}`, formatted as the Watch button's `onClick` is.
   - In `TogetherRoute`, directly after `const [watching, setWatching] = …`, add `const challengeOpener = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);`. It must come before the `if (watching !== null)` early return, because hooks may not follow it.
   - After the `act` function and before `if (watching !== null)`, add:
     ```ts
     /**
      * Closes the challenge dialog and gives the focus back to the Challenge button that opened it, as a
      * dialog should leave it (WAI-ARIA APG; `Game.tsx`'s `refocusConcede`). The button is kept when it is
      * pressed, not read off the focus, which a click on a button does not move in every browser.
      */
     const closeChallenge = (): void => {
       setChallenging(null);
       const opener = challengeOpener.current;
       challengeOpener.current = null;
       if (opener !== null && opener.isConnected) opener.focus({ preventScroll: true });
     };
     ```
   - In the `<FriendRow …>` map, set `onChallenge={(opener) => { challengeOpener.current = opener; setChallenging({ profileId: friend.profileId, username: friend.username }); }}`.
   - On `<ChallengeDialog>`, set `onClose={closeChallenge}` and make `onSent` run `closeChallenge(); reloadChallenges();`.

3. **`apps/web/src/together/InMatchChat.tsx`.**
   - Change the import to `import { useId, useRef, useState, type ReactElement } from "react";`.
   - In `InMatchChat`, after `const [chatWith, setChatWith] = …`, add `const toggle = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);` and `const listId = useId();`.
   - On the toggle button, add `ref={toggle}` and, after `aria-expanded={open}`, `aria-controls={open ? listId : undefined}`.
   - On `<div className="in-match-chat__list" …>`, add `id={listId}`.
   - In the `ChatPanel`'s `onClose`, after `reloadUnread();`, add:
     ```ts
     // The friend picked left with the list, so the focus goes back to the toggle that opened both.
     toggle.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
     ```

4. **`apps/web/src/emotes/PortraitPicker.tsx`.**
   - Add `useId` to the `react` import.
   - `PortraitTile`: add the prop `panelId: string` to the destructuring, after `previewing`, and to the type, with the doc comment `/** The id of the picker's one preview panel, which this tile's Preview shows while \`previewing\`. */`. On the Preview button, after `aria-expanded={previewing}`, add `aria-controls={previewing ? panelId : undefined}`.
   - `PortraitPicker`: after `const root = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);`, add:
     - `const toggle = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);`
     - `const menuId = useId();`
     - `const panelId = useId();`
   - Extend the comment above the close effect with: "Escape gives the focus back to the portrait button unless the player has put it elsewhere on the page (#1569); an outside press leaves it where the press put it."
   - Replace that effect's `onKeyDown` body with:
     ```ts
     if (event.key !== "Escape") return;
     setOpen(false);
     const focused = document.activeElement;
     if (focused === null || focused === document.body || root.current?.contains(focused) === true) {
       toggle.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
     }
     ```
     Leave `onPointerDown` unchanged.
   - On the `portrait-current` button, add `ref={toggle}` and, after `aria-expanded={open}`, `aria-controls={open ? menuId : undefined}`.
   - On `<div className="portrait-menu" …>`, add `id={menuId}`. On `<div className="portrait-preview" …>`, add `id={panelId}`.
   - In the tiles map, pass `panelId={panelId}`. In its `onPick`, after `setOpen(false);`, add:
     ```ts
     // The tile goes with the menu, so the focus goes back to the portrait button (#1569).
     toggle.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
     ```

## Tests

**`apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.test.tsx`**

Setup:
- Add `import { stopFollowingChallenge } from "./follow.ts";` after the `./config.ts` import.
- Add to `TESTID`:
  - `challengeForm: "together-challenge-form"`
  - `challengeModeBo1: "together-challenge-mode-bo1"`
  - `challengeDeck: "together-challenge-deck"`
  - `challengeSend: "together-challenge-send"`
  - `challengeClose: "together-challenge-close"`
- Before `const IN_MATCH`, add `stats.test.tsx`'s `press(key, options)` helper, as `fireEvent.keyDown(document.activeElement ?? document.body, { key, ...options })`.
- At the end of the file, add `describe("the challenge dialog's focus (#1569)")`. Its helper `openChallenge()` runs `fireEvent.click` on `within(rowOf(ANN)).getByTestId(TESTID.challenge)` and returns that button. `fireEvent.click` leaves the focus where it was, as Safari does.

The four tests, each starting with `await renderPage()`:
1. **"opening it takes the focus to its checked mode, and Escape closes it from anywhere and gives the focus back to the Challenge button"**
   - The form has `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`, and the `challengeModeBo1` radio has the focus.
   - Then `(document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null)?.blur(); press("Escape")`.
   - The form is gone and the Challenge button has the focus.
2. **"keeps Tab and Shift+Tab on its controls, the mode group one stop, and brings them back inside from the page behind"**
   - `await screen.findByTestId(TESTID.challengeDeck, undefined, SLOW)`.
   - Tab goes mode → deck → send → cancel → mode. Shift+Tab then goes to cancel, then to send.
   - Focus `TESTID.addInput`: Tab lands on mode. Focus it again: Shift+Tab lands on cancel.
3. **"closes on a click on the scrim, never on one inside it, and on Cancel, each time giving the focus back to the Challenge button"**
   - A click on the form leaves it open.
   - A click on `must(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".together-dialog-scrim"), "the scrim")` closes it, and the Challenge button has the focus.
   - `openChallenge()` again, then `expect(challenge).not.toHaveFocus()`. A click on `challengeClose` closes it, and the Challenge button has the focus.
4. **"a sent challenge closes it and gives the focus back to the Challenge button"**
   - Start with `renderPage(world(), (call) => call.method === "POST" && call.path === "/api/challenges" ? { status: 201, body: { challengeId: "ch-1", roomCode: "ROOM01" } } : undefined)`.
   - Wait for the deck select, then click `challengeSend`.
   - `waitFor` the form to be gone, with `SLOW`. Then the Challenge button has the focus and `server.to("POST", "/api/challenges")` has length 1.
   - End with `stopFollowingChallenge()`.

**`apps/web/src/together/ChatPanel.test.tsx`**

In `describe("B58 the in-match chat toggle")`, before "B58 the toggle does not list offline friends", add **"B58 closing the conversation, by its close control or by Escape, gives the focus back to the toggle, which names its list while open"**:
- `serveFriends(); render(<InMatchChat />)`, and get `toggle` by testid `in-match-chat-toggle`. It has no `aria-controls`.
- Click it. Its `aria-controls` equals `screen.getByTestId("in-match-chat-list").id`.
- Click Ann's button, `must((await screen.findByText(wholeText("Ann#2"), undefined, SLOW)).closest("button"), "Ann's button")`. The input `chat-input` (found with `findByTestId`) has the focus, and the toggle has no `aria-controls`.
- Click `chat-close`. The panel `chat-panel` is gone and the toggle has the focus.
- Click the toggle and Ann again, then `fireEvent.keyDown(await screen.findByTestId("chat-input", undefined, SLOW), { key: "Escape" })`. The panel is gone and the toggle has the focus.

**`apps/web/src/emotes/PortraitPicker.test.tsx`**

Before `describe("the emote previews (R644)")`, add `describe("the picker gives the focus back (#1569)")` with these tests, using the file's `picker()` and `openPicker()`:
1. **"Escape from inside the menu closes it and gives the focus back to the portrait button, which names the menu only while it is open"**
   - Before opening, `portrait-current` has no `aria-controls`. After opening, it has `aria-controls` equal to `menu.id`, which is not `""`.
   - Focus `portrait-pick-timmy` and `fireEvent.keyDown` Escape on it.
   - No dialog, `portrait-current` has the focus and no `aria-controls`.
2. **"a pick closes the menu and gives the focus back to the portrait button"**
   - Focus and then click `portrait-pick-felinors`.
   - `onPick` was called with `"felinors"`, there is no dialog, and `portrait-current` has the focus.
3. **"a press outside, or Escape once the focus is elsewhere on the page, leaves the focus where the player put it"**
   - Render `<><button type="button" data-testid="elsewhere">elsewhere</button>{picker("gary")}</>`.
   - Open, focus `elsewhere`, `fireEvent.pointerDown(elsewhere)`: closed, and `elsewhere` has the focus.
   - Open, focus `elsewhere`, `fireEvent.keyDown(elsewhere, { key: "Escape" })`: closed, and `elsewhere` has the focus.
4. **"each portrait's Preview names the preview panel while it shows that portrait's pool"**
   - `portrait-preview-gary` has no `aria-controls`. Click it.
   - It has `aria-expanded="true"` and `aria-controls` equal to `portrait-preview-panel`'s `id`, which is not `""`. `portrait-preview-timmy` has no `aria-controls`.

**Run:**
```
sh scripts/build-wasm.sh
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/together/TogetherRoute.test.tsx src/together/ChatPanel.test.tsx src/emotes/PortraitPicker.test.tsx
pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts'
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e
```

## Done when

- [ ] The challenge dialog focuses its checked mode on open, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, Escape closes it with the focus anywhere, and every close returns the focus to the Challenge button.
- [ ] Escape or a pick in the portrait picker returns the focus to `portrait-current`, and closing the in-match chat returns it to `in-match-chat-toggle`.
- [ ] `aria-controls` is on the three `aria-expanded` toggles while they are expanded.
- [ ] The 9 new tests pass, and so do the three files' existing tests.
- [ ] The harness's web tests, the web typecheck and eslint are green. `cargo fmt --check` and the other Rust checks are unaffected, since there is no Rust change.

## Risks

- **The submit flow.** Only the form's `onKeyDown` is removed and `onSubmit` is untouched. Test 4 sends a challenge end to end, and e2e `42-together.cy.ts` uses the same testids.
- **The opener can vanish.** If the friend goes in-game or offline while the dialog is open, polling unmounts their Challenge button, and the `isConnected` check then leaves the focus alone. `closeChallenge` clears the ref, so a send that resolves after an Escape doesn't pull the focus back later.
- **The key listener re-subscribes.** It is window-capture and its deps are `[onClose]`, which is a new function on every `TogetherRoute` render. Re-subscribing is harmless. Do not move the focus-on-open into that effect, or it would refocus on every poll. Escape's `stopPropagation` keeps an open `ChatPanel` from also closing.
- **Hidden information and determinism.** Neither is touched: this is the client only, with no engine change.

## Open questions

Decisions this plan made that the issue left open, with the rejected alternatives:
1. **`useModalOverlay` (`cards/inspect/store.ts`) is not reused.** Rejected because it reads the opener off `document.activeElement` (a click doesn't focus a button in Safari), and its `trapTab` lets the browser's own Tab run from a mid-dialog stop, which leaves the dialog from a non-first radio. The plan copies `ConfirmConcede.tsx`'s window handler instead.
2. **The first focus goes to the checked mode radio, not the form.** Making the form focusable was rejected; it would need `tabIndex={-1}` and a focus ring.
3. **The restore lives in the callers**, as `Game.tsx`'s `refocusConcede` does, not in `ChallengeDialog` or `ChatPanel`. The in-match friend button unmounts as the panel opens, so `ChatPanel` could not find it.
4. **The portrait picker restores on Escape only when the focus is in the picker or nowhere, and never on an outside press.**
5. **`aria-controls` is set only while expanded**, so it never points at an id that isn't rendered.
6. **Left out:** `/together`'s own Chat button. It opens `ChatPanel` and still loses the focus on close; the issue asks only for the in-match chat. Whether to fix it is a follow-up a person can decide.
````
